title: Fonctions L / Équation fonctionnelle des fonctions L (cas géométrique) : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: the cote is about the functional equation of L-functions in the geometric (function field) case. This page records how the L-function behaves under the tensor and λ-operations on its argument. The ring in question is the big Witt ring W(Λ) = 1 + tΛ[[t]], with Λ presumably an ℓ-adic coefficient ring. 'Addition' in W(Λ) is multiplication of power series. Multiplication * is defined by (1−at)*(1−bt) = 1−abt. The special λ-structure is given by λ^p(∏(1−λ_i t)) = ∏_{i1<…<ip}(1−λ_{i1}…λ_{ip} t). The quotes around 'la' signal that a choice (normalisation) of λ-structure is being made.

For an object f (most naturally a finite-dimensional space with Frobenius endomorphism, or a cohomology object), P_f(t) = det(1 − tF | f) is the characteristic polynomial. L_f is the alternating combination over degrees, L_f = ∏ P_{f,i}^{(−1)^{i+1}}; additively, L_f = −Σ(−1)^i P_i.

Step 1 (tensor products). By eigenvalue multiplication, P_{f⊗f'} = P_f * P_{f'}. Via a Künneth decomposition P_n(f⊗f') = Σ_{i+j=n} P_i(f)*P_j(f'), so L_{f⊗f'} = Σ(−1)^{i+j+1}P_i*P_j = −(L_f*L_{f'}). Multiplicatively this is 1/(L_f*L_{f'}). For p factors one gets (∏^* L_{f_i})^{(−1)^{p+1}}, with ∏^* the Witt product.

Step 2 (λ-operations). P_{λ^i f} = λ^i P_f, so f ↦ 1/L_f = −L_f is a λ-ring homomorphism into W(Λ). Hence −L_{λ^i f} = λ^i(−L_f). In generating-series form, Σ(−L_{λ^i f})s^i = λ_s(−L_f) = λ_s(L_f)^{−1} = σ_{−s}(L_f) = Σ(−1)^i σ^i(L_f)s^i. Here σ_s(x) = λ_{−s}(x)^{−1}.

Conclusion: L_{λ^i f} = (σ^i L_f)^{(−1)^{i+1}}, and symmetrically L_{σ^i f} = (λ^i L_f)^{(−1)^{i+1}}. The crossed-out line was a first attempt at the identity λ_s(x)·σ_{−s}(x) = 1, written via the unit [1/(1−t)] of W.

Purpose: bookkeeping lemmas showing that the L-function is a (sign-twisted) λ-ring homomorphism from a Grothendieck group of Frobenius-objects/complexes to W(Λ). The degree shift accounts for the sign. These are presumably preparatory to expressing L-functions of tensor and symmetric/exterior constructions in the functional-equation argument.
errors: Sign juggling is visible: several (−1)^i and (−s) factors are written and then struck out. The final boxed formulas L_{λ^i f} = (σ^i L_f)^{(−1)^{i+1}} and L_{σ^i f} = (λ^i L_f)^{(−1)^{i+1}} are correct under the convention L = −(Euler characteristic of P's) in W(Λ).
The tensor formula requires a Künneth decomposition (or that f, f' be graded objects over a point). This is not stated on the page.
The intermediate equality '= Σ σ^i(L_f) s^i' lacks the (−1)^i signs unless s is replaced by −s. This is a harmless slip, corrected implicitly in the final formulas.

ideas.what: Characteristic polynomials / L-functions viewed as elements of the big Witt ring 1+tΛ[[t]], with tensor product corresponding to Witt multiplication
ideas.modern_name: Characteristic-polynomial map K_0(End) → W(Λ) (rational Witt vectors); zeta functions as Witt vectors
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (λ-rings, 1957) for the Witt-type λ-ring 1+tA[[t]]; Almkvist (1974/78) for K_0(End) ≅ rational Witt vectors; later Ramachandran et al. for zeta functions as Witt vectors
ideas.where_published: The λ-ring 1+tA[[t]] appears in Grothendieck's Riemann–Roch / λ-ring theory (Berthelot–Grothendieck–Illusie, SGA 6). The explicit L-function statement is unsure.

ideas.what: L-function of exterior/symmetric powers: L_{λ^i f} = (σ^i L_f)^{±1}, L_{σ^i f} = (λ^i L_f)^{±1}, from λ_s(−x) = σ_{−s}(x)
ideas.modern_name: λ-ring homomorphism property of the zeta/L map with degree-shift sign (λ^i(−x) = (−1)^iσ^i(x))
ideas.usually_credited_to: Folklore in λ-ring theory; standard in later work on motivic zeta functions (Kapranov, Larsen–Lunts, Ramachandran)

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a clean but routine computation: the L-function is a sign-twisted λ-homomorphism into the big Witt ring. This is standard λ-ring formalism that Grothendieck himself introduced. The early date (possibly 1960s, before Almkvist's K_0(End) results) is mildly interesting historically. The mathematics itself is well known.
